articles.title: Accelerating operational excellence in offshore energy
articles.summary: By- Nisha Lathif, General Manager, Oil and Gas,Honeywell Technologies With decades of expertise in addressing the complex needs of the energy...
articles.body: Branded Content October 27, 2026 · 15 hours ago Accelerating operational excellence in offshore energy Written in partnership with Honeywell Technologies 6 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Integrated offshore solutions by Honeywell Technologies @Honeywell Technologies By- Nisha Lathif, General Manager, Oil and Gas,Honeywell Technologies With decades of expertise in addressing the complex needs of the energy sector in challenging marine environments, Honeywell Technologies is at the heart of shaping the future of offshore energy operations. Our advances are supporting a fundamental shift in the industry, helping transform traditional offshore operations into becoming more connected, intelligent and data driven. As digital technologies continue to evolve, we see that operators can leverage real-time data, advanced analytics and integrated operational platforms to gain deeper insights into asset performance and operational efficiency. This shift is enabling organizations to make more informed decisions, optimize maintenance and production strategies and create more agile, resilient offshore operations. Offshore operations are entering a new era Offshore energy operators are confronting a convergence of pressures that traditional ways of working were never designed to handle. Aging infrastructure is becoming a primary constraint today. While equipment ages, operational complexity continues to increase, experienced offshore professionals are becoming harder to replace and the pressure to improve reliability and safety while managing costs remains high. 4,5 The key to solving many of these challenges can be found in data. Modern offshore facilities generate massive volumes of operational data. Historically, much of this information was underutilized, trapped in individual systems or available only after issues had already occurred. Some operators are now moving beyond traditional maintenance strategies to embrace digital technologies that enable smarter, faster operational decision-making. The organizations making the greatest progress are those that convert operational data into actionable intelligence. Rather than simply collecting information, they are using analytics and connected systems to identify risks earlier, optimize maintenance activities and improve operational performance before failures impact production. Why predictive operations matter Reactive and time-based maintenance have clear limitations. Waiting for equipment to fail means unplanned downtime, lost production and elevated safety risk. Servicing equipment on a fixed calendar schedule, regardless of actual condition, wastes resources and can compromise assets through unnecessary intervention. Condition-based maintenance (CBM) offers a proactive alternative, focusing on real-time monitoring rather than adherence to fixed schedules. Operational and equipment data are continuously monitored to assess actual asset health. By combining real-time monitoring with advanced analytics, operators can identify emerging issues before they develop into significant failures. The benefits of this approach are substantial: · Reduced unplanned downtime · Better maintenance prioritization · Improved equipment availability · Reduced operational risk · Enhanced workforce productivity By assessing the actual state of equipment, operators can conduct maintenance only when conditions warrant it, effectively reducing unnecessary downtime and optimizing resource allocation. CBM moves beyond simple data collection. When data, analytics and human expertise are connected, operators gain the ability to move from reacting to problems toward anticipating and preventing them. That helps people make faster, better decisions. Aker BP: A case study of CBM in offshore operations 2, 3 Aker BP, a leading energy exploration and production company operating on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, offers a practical illustration of CBM in action. Like many offshore producers, their challenges included managing equipment reliability and conducting maintenance across multiple offshore assets while maintaining high safety standards and operational efficiency. To overcome these challenges Aker BP adopted condition-based maintenance using Honeywell Technologies Forge Asset Performance Management (APM), a connected platform that integrates real-time data from multiple equipment types and original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) into a single dashboard, creating a unified, OEM-agnostic approach to asset health monitoring that facilitates proactive decision-making. With Honeywell Technologies Forge APM now providing enterprise-wide control, Aker BP can continuously monitor equipment conditions on six of its assets in the North Sea, ensuring that maintenance is carried out only when necessary. Aker BP reports that the real benefits of using CBM strategies have been meaningful: · Earlier identification of equipment issues · Reduced dependence on manual inspections · Better prioritization of maintenance activities · Improved situational awareness In addition, equipment essential for safety—such as safety valves, pressure sensors and critical control systems — receives focused attention based on its operational status. The new approach also carries clear safety benefits for Aker BP. By reducing the frequency of scheduled maintenance (some of it unnecessary), CBM minimizes disruptions to their ongoing operations, thereby decreasing the chances of accidents during maintenance activities. The advantages gained were not simply from software deployment. Dedicated ownership and continuous refinement were also essential. Experienced technicians at Aker BP set up their own models in the system specifically for their required calculations. They engaged ongoing improvement and adaptation to the monitoring process that allowed engineers to tune the system more effectively, minimize false alerts and concentrate on critical issues. This is a reminder that predictive maintenance is fundamentally a new operating model. Success requires connected data, advanced analytics and experienced personnel working together to make better decisions. Technology provides visibility and insight, but operational excellence still depends on informed human judgment. Lessons for the offshore industry The Aker BP experience points to several broader ideals for the offshore industry: · Connect data across systems. Operators need a unified view instead of isolated monitoring tools. Integrating data from multiple equipment types and OEMs into a single dashboard enables proactive decision-making. · Focus on actionable insights. The goal is not more alerts—the goal is better decisions. Minimizing false alerts keeps attention on critical issues. · Combine technology and expertise . Analytics support engineers, but people remain central to decision-making. · Create a culture of continuous improvement. Condition-monitoring systems become more valuable as teams refine models and operating practices over time. Building the offshore operation of the future Putting these ideals into practice to create future-ready offshore operations requires an integrated operating environment that connects production systems, assets, people, safety functions and sustainability objectives. Honeywell Technologies engages in all aspects of transforming offshore operations through six connected domains that collectively support safer, more efficient and more resilient offshore production. For the operational foundation we bring operations and control capabilities, including SCADA, process control, telemetry and connectivity that provide visibility across offshore assets. We enable digital transformation technologies such as Industrial IoT, predictive analytics, AI-enabled operations and digital twins to help organizations transform data into operational intelligence. Honeywell Technologies asset performance solutions support reliability and optimization through asset performance management platforms, turbomachinery optimization, measurement technologies and energy management capabilities. Our people and collaboration technologies enable remote operations, expert collaboration, knowledge management and workforce training, addressing the growing workforce challenges across offshore operations. Our safety and security systems integrate process safety, cybersecurity, and fire and gas systems into a unified operational environment. We compliment these with sustainability solutions that incorporate emissions monitoring, energy optimization and carbon management capabilities. The entire portfolio of Honeywell Technologies’ offshore production capabilities creates a connected operational ecosystem where data flows across functions, enabling faster decisions, improved efficiency and greater resilience. The next frontier of operational excellence As the Aker BP example demonstrates, the real value of offshore operational excellence lies not in technology alone, but in transforming operational data into actionable insights. By connecting assets, people and processes within a unified operational environment, operators can improve reliability, enhance efficiency and support safer operations. As the industry evolves, condition-based maintenance and predictive analytics will continue to play a key role in building more resilient and high-performing offshore operations. articles.body: Americas Offshore Chouest Group acquires Canada’s Horizon Maritime Bojan Lepic October 27, 2026 0 670 1 minute read Horizon Maritime Horizon Maritime US offshore services giant Chouest Group has acquired Canadian marine and offshore services provider Horizon Maritime, expanding its presence across Canada’s east and west coasts and into the Arctic. The Louisiana-based group has partnered with Horizon Maritime’s founders to acquire the St. John’s-headquartered company from CFFI and its lender HPS. The transaction’s financial details were not disclosed. The acquisition combines Chouest’s global offshore support fleet, subsea services, shipbuilding, specialised engineering, and marine technology capabilities with Horizon’s operations in Canada’s offshore energy and harsh-environment markets. The companies said the combination would let Horizon expand across all three Canadian coastlines, giving customers access to a broader range of marine transportation, subsea, and offshore services. Horizon Maritime will retain its existing management and leadership structure, with Steve Widmeyer continuing as chief executive. Widmeyer and company co-founder Sean Leet will also join the board of directors. Founded in 2015, Horizon Maritime operates in offshore energy, Arctic logistics, and specialised marine services. Its fleet includes the anchor-handling tug supply vessel Horizon Arctic , the platform supply vessel Horizon Dragon , and the icebreaker Polar Prince , along with three smaller utility tugs designed for operations in icy waters. The company also operates a Canadian harbour towage joint venture with Dutch towage specialist Kotug, established in 2019. articles.body: Europe Offshore Eni locks in offshore contractors for Cyprus gas project Bojan Lepic October 27, 2026 0 408 1 minute read Eni Eni Italian energy major Eni has signed the main engineering, procurement, construction, and drilling contracts for the Cronos gas development offshore Cyprus, with a string of major offshore contractors securing work on the project. The contracts, valued by local media at around $1.8bn, mark the start of the development’s execution phase in Block 6, following a final investment decision by Eni and partner TotalEnergies in July. Although Eni did not disclose the contractors involved, local media identified eight companies awarded work on the development, covering subsea production systems, pipelines, offshore installation, drilling and associated infrastructure. Baker Hughes will design, procure, and construct subsea production systems, while TechnipFMC will supply flexible gas production lines. Dalmine has been selected to supply gas export and monoethylene glycol pipelines, with Oceaneering International responsible for subsea umbilicals and control systems. China Merchants Heavy Industry will design, construct, transport, and install a floating control unit. US offshore engineering contractor McDermott will handle offshore transportation, installation, tie-ins, and commissioning of subsea pipelines and equipment. McDermott had already announced a contract worth between $500m and $750m for Cronos in September, marking its first subsea project award from Eni. Egyptian contractor Petrojet will construct a new onshore gas pipeline connecting the Zohr facilities with the Damietta LNG terminal, while Italy’s Saipem has been selected to provide drilling services using its Saipem 10000 drillship. Separately, Halliburton secured a bundled well construction and completions contract for Cronos in September, covering drilling fluids, directional drilling, cementing, automation, and other well services. The Cronos development will involve four subsea wells targeting resources estimated at more than 3trn cubic feet of gas initially in place. Production is expected to begin in the first half of 2028, reaching a plateau of up to 500m standard cubic feet per day. Gas will be transported to Egypt for processing through existing Zohr-field infrastructure before being liquefied at Damietta for export, primarily to European markets. Eni operates Block 6 with a 50% stake, while TotalEnergies holds the remaining interest. articles.body: Middle East Operations Asyad Group prices $132m shipping stake sale Adis Ajdin October 27, 2026 0 417 1 minute read Asyad Shipping Asyad Shipping Oman’s Asyad Group has priced an institutional share sale in its listed shipping subsidiary at OMR50.8m ($132m), reducing its ownership as part of a move to broaden the company’s shareholder base. Muscat-listed Asyad Shipping said the institutional bookbuilding process closed heavily oversubscribed. The transaction covers 5% of Asyad Shipping’s issued share capital. Upon completion, the company’s free float will rise to 25%, meeting the minimum requirement set by Oman’s Financial Services Authority. The shares are being sold by parent Asyad Group, which will receive the proceeds. No new shares are being issued, and Asyad Shipping will not receive any of the funds. The group is also preparing a separate retail offering of up to 1.25% of the shipping company at the same price, subject to regulatory approval. Settlement and listing of the institutional shares are expected on November 4. The remaining shares held by Asyad Group will be subject to a 180-day lock-up following settlement. The transaction follows Asyad Shipping’s March 2025 initial public offering, which raised approximately $333m and brought 20% of the company into public ownership. Since listing, the company has continued expanding and renewing its fleet across the tanker, dry bulk, gas and container sectors. Asyad operated a fleet of 91 vessels at the end of June, including 48 owned or co-owned ships, 31 chartered-in vessels and 12 newbuildings. Its latest investment programme includes eight charter-backed MR product tankers ordered at HD Hyundai and three VLCCs contracted at Hanwha Ocean earlier this year. The company has also been recycling capital through secondhand sales. In September, it agreed to dispose of three ageing tankers for a combined OMR68.44m ($178m), including two VLCCs. articles.title: Dolphin Drilling parts ways with 52-year-old rig and forges pact with SPM
articles.summary: Dolphin Drilling has sealed a deal to divest its 1974-built rig for up to $25 million and formed a strategic partnership with SPM.
articles.body: Business & Finance October 27, 2026 · 17 hours ago Dolphin Drilling parts ways with 52-year-old rig and forges pact with SPM Dolphin Drilling has sealed a deal to divest its 1974-built rig for up to $25 million and formed a strategic partnership with SPM. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 4 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Blackford Dolphin rig; Source: Dolphin Drilling Dolphin Drilling, an Oslo-listed, Aberdeen-headquartered owner and operator of a fleet of harsh-environment mid-water and deepwater semi-submersible drilling rigs, has taken a step to strengthen its financial position, offloading its semi-submersible rig for $25 million in a transaction expected to close next month in Singapore, while partnering with SPM Energy Shipping FZCO to capture upside in a tightening global rig market. Dolphin Drilling has entered into a definitive sale and purchase agreement (SPA) for the sale of the 1974-built Blackford Dolphin semi-submersible rig with SPM for a total consideration of $25 million, comprising $10 million, payable upon delivery of the rig and $15 million, payable when SPM receives the first payment under a potential future drilling contract. The sale is expected to close on or about November 5, 2026, in Singapore, immediately and materially reducing the firm’s operating cost base, eliminating the class renewal survey capital expenditures related to this rig and significantly strengthening the company’s financial position. The duo has also entered into a memorandum of understanding (MoU) for the management of future drilling contracts for this rig and one additional semi-submersible, as well as any other rigs or units that the two companies may agree upon. The company explains that these management arrangements contemplate entry into management agreements and other deals, which remain subject to definitive documentation and customary closing conditions. The contemplated management arrangements combine Dolphin Drilling’s established operating platform, technical expertise and long track record with the strong commercial presence of the participating companies in India and the surrounding regions. The rigs will be marketed by SPM in India and other areas agreed upon between the two players, with capital costs, operational expenses and guarantees related to future drilling contracts to be covered by SPM as owners of the rigs. Ronny Bjørnådal , Chairman of the Board of Directors of Dolphin Drilling, commented: “Dolphin Drilling will through the sale and contemplated management arrangements materially de-risk the company and at the same time, significantly reduce operating costs as well as eliminate capital expenditures associated with the class renewal survey for the Blackford Dolphin. “The transactions provide for potential future upside through management of Blackford Dolphin and one or more additional semi-submersible drilling rig resulting in future management fees and ability to grow our platform.” Related Articles Fossil Energy Dolphin Drilling: GHL cash-and-rig proposal ‘encouraging’ but settlement offer falls short 2 min read Dolphin Drilling believes the sale and management arrangements offer a compelling combination of immediate risk reduction and value realization while preserving exposure to the potential upside from improving offshore drilling market fundamentals and a further tightening of the supply and demand balance. The transactions are highly attractive to the company, as they are expected to reduce the company’s interest-bearing debt and its capital expenditures related to Blackford Dolphin while creating opportunities for future revenue generation from the semi-submersible and other rigs under management, complementing the firm’s existing operating model with capital-light revenue streams. Bjørnådal emphasized: “The management arrangements would combine SPM’s commercial capabilities, market access and relationships in some of the most active benign-water markets in the world with Dolphin Drilling’s established operating platform, technical expertise and worldwide operating licenses, a proven operating platform and decades of experience. “This gives us the flexibility to capture the prospective upside of a tightening rig market, while strengthening our platform and driving long-term shareholder value.” The strategic partnership aligns well with Dolphin Drilling’s broader, ongoing evaluation of strategic initiatives and business opportunities to participate in industry consolidation and further growth. The company reported at the end of second quarter 2026 improved financial figures, including total cash of $55.1 million and a firm revenue contracted backlog of $556 million, with a further $446 million in options, resulting from multi-year contracts secured for Paul B. Loyd Jr. and Borgland Dolphin . Related Articles Fossil Energy UK oil & gas operator hires Dolphin Drilling’s rig on multimillion-dollar gig 2 min read The offshore drilling contractor underlines that its current contract backlog, combined with the sale of Blackford Dolphin and the potential management arrangements, further enhances its financial stability and long-term outlook. The firm underlines that it is well positioned to continue to evaluate and pursue strategic initiatives aimed at enhancing long-term shareholder value, including organic growth opportunities, following the sale of this rig and the strategic partnership with SPM and their marketing consultant Valiant Oil and Gas (VOG) through the management arrangements. Dolphin Drilling noted: “The market for semi-submersible drilling rigs, the segment in which Dolphin Drilling’s fleet operates, remains tight. Years of limited newbuild activity, combined with the retirement and scrapping of older units, have significantly reduced the available supply of moored floaters, and there is no newbuild pipeline to replenish the fleet. “At the same time, demand is supported by a renewed focus on energy security and increased investments in offshore developments, including in benign-water regions such as India, Southeast Asia, Mexico and West Africa. articles.body: Dry Cargo Greater China Shipyards Zijin Mining orders bulker pair for African mineral trade Adis Ajdin October 27, 2026 0 618 1 minute read Xinneng Shipbuilding Xinneng Shipbuilding Chinese mining giant Zijin Mining has returned to Shandong Xinneng Shipbuilding for two 3,000 dwt bulk carriers, expanding its dedicated mineral transport operation on Lake Tanganyika in eastern Africa. The latest contract follows an earlier order for four 2,000 dwt vessels at the same Chinese yard, which are now operating on the lake between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Tanzania. The new ships will be 50% larger than their predecessors, adding a combined 6,000 dwt to Zijin’s lake transport capacity. Contract value and delivery dates have not been disclosed. The investment forms part of Zijin’s efforts to establish an alternative export corridor for minerals from its operations in the DRC. The group’s existing shipping operation links Congolese cargoes with Kigoma in Tanzania, from where they can move towards the country’s Indian Ocean export infrastructure. Zijin’s first four lake bulkers were built through an arrangement that saw hull sections manufactured in China and assembled in Tanzania, overcoming the logistical challenges of building vessels for an African inland waterway. The company established the route to support its growing mining interests in central Africa and reduce dependence on existing overland transport connections. articles.body: Interconnectors October 27, 2026 · 17 hours ago Fugro's 18-meter USV on survey duty at 'world's longest interconnector' NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 1 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Blue Eclipse. Source: Fugro Fugro's 18-meter Blue Eclipse uncrewed surface vessel (USV) is carrying out an environmental survey for the 1.4 GW Viking Link high-voltage direct current (DC) electricity link between the British and Danish transmission systems, said to be the world's longest interconnector. According to the National Grid's Notice to Mariners (NtM) issued on October 8, Blue Eclipse was scheduled to start the operations on October 22 and continue until November 10, subject to prevailing weather conditions and work progress. The environmental camera survey is being performed in the North Sea from the nearshore limit north of the Viking Link cable, northeast of Mablethorpe, Lincolnshire, and extending offshore to the UK/Netherlands border. The survey works shall provide seabed imagery along 193 selected 100m transects along the route. Blue Eclipse is being operated from a remote operations center (ROC) in Aberdeen. Viking Link is approximately 765 kilometers long and connects the Bicker Fen substation in Lincolnshire and the Revsing substation in southern Jutland, Denmark.
